The glorious success of the gospel among the Jews after Christ's ascension began by that pouring [out] of the Spirit, which began at Pentecost, that we read of [in Acts 2].[^004-note1386] So wonderful was this pouring out ‹of the Spirit›, and so remarkable and swift the effect of it, that we read of three thousand that were converted to the Christian faith in one day, Acts 2:41. And probably the bigger part of these were savingly converted. And after this, we read of God's adding to the church "daily such as should be saved," Acts 2:47; and soon after we read that the number of them was about five thousand.[^004-note1387] Thus were not only a multitude converted, but the church was then eminent in piety, as appears by Acts 2:46–47 ["And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house.… Praising God"].[^004-note1388] And Acts 4:32 ["And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul … they had all things common"].

Thus the Christian church was first of all of the nation of Israel, and therefore when the Gentiles were called they were but, as it were, added to Israel, to the seed of Abraham. They were added to the Christian church of Israel as the proselytes of old were to the Mosaic

<!-- p. 377 -->

church of Israel, and so were, as it were, only grafted on to the stock of Abraham and were not a distinct tree; for they are all still the seed of Abraham and Israel, as Ruth the Moabitess, and Uriah the Hittite, and other proselytes of old were the same people and received as the seed of Israel.[^004-note1389]

So the Christian church at first began at Jerusalem, and from thence was propagated to all nations, so that this church of Jerusalem was the church that was, as it were, the mother of all other churches in the world, agreeable to the prophecy, Isaiah 2:3–4, "The law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the Lord [from Jerusalem]. And he shall judge among the nations and rebuke [many people]."[^004-note1390] So that the whole church of God is still God's Jerusalem: they are his spiritual[^004-note1391] Jerusalem and are, as it were, only added to the church that was begun in the literal Jerusalem. After this we read of many thousands of Jews that believed in Jerusalem, Acts 21:20 ["Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe"]. And so we read of multitudes of Jews that were converted in other cities of Judea, and not only so, but in other parts of the world. For wherever[^004-note1392] the apostles went, if there were any Jews there, their manner was first to go into the synagogues of the Jews and preach the gospel to them; and many in one place and another believed, as in Damascus and Antioch and many other places that we read of in the Acts.[^004-note1393]

In this pouring out of the Spirit, which began at the Pentecost following Christ's ascension, began that first great dispensation ‹which is called Christ's coming in his kingdom›. Christ's coming thus in a spiritual manner for the glorious setting up his kingdom in the world, is represented by Christ himself as his coming down from heaven whither he had ascended, John 14:18. There Christ, having been speaking of his ascension, says, "I will not leave you comfortless: I will come unto you,"[^004-note1394] speaking of his coming by the coming of the comforter, the spirit of truth. And John 14:28, "Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you." And thus the

<!-- p. 378 -->

apostles began to see the kingdom of God come with power, as he promised they should, Mark 9:1, "Verily I say [unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power]."

2.[^004-note1395] What is nextly to be observed is the success of the gospel among the Samaritans. After the success of the gospel had been so gloriously begun among the proper Jews, the Spirit of God was, nextly, wonderfully poured out on the Samaritans, which were not Jews by nation but the posterity [of those settled in the land that was inhabited by the ten tribes].[^004-note1396] But yet they had received the five books of Moses, and practiced most of the rites of the law of Moses, and so were a sort of mongrel Jews. We don't find 'em reckoned as Gentiles in the New Testament, for the calling of the Gentiles is spoken of as a new thing after this, beginning with the conversion of Cornelius.[^004-note1397] But yet it was an instance of making these[^004-note1398] a people that were not a people, for they corrupted the religion that Moses commanded, and did not go up to Jerusalem to worship, but had another temple of their own on Mount Gerizim, which is the mountain that the woman of Samaria speaks of when she says, "Our fathers worshipped [in this mountain]."[^004-note1399] Christ there don't approve of their separation from the Jews, but tells the woman of Samaria that they worshipped they knew not what, and that salvation was of the Jews.[^004-note1400]

But now salvation is brought from the Jews to them by the preaching of Philip, excepting that before Christ had some success, with whose preaching there was a glorious pouring out of the Spirit of God in the city of Samaria, where we are told that, "The people believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of Christ, and were baptized, both men and women," and that "there was great joy in that city," Acts 8:8–12.[^004-note1401] Thus Christ had a glorious harvest in Samaria, which is what Christ seems to have had respect to in what he said to his disciples at Jacob's well three or four years before, on occasion[^004-note1402] of the people of Samaria's appearing at a distance in the fields, coming to the place where Christ was at the instigation

<!-- p. 379 -->

of the woman of Samaria. On that occasion he bids his disciples lift up their eyes to the fields, John 4:35–36 ["… for they are white already to harvest. And he that reapeth … gathereth fruit unto life eternal"]. The disposition that the people of Samaria showed towards Christ and his gospel, showed them that this people were ripe to the harvest. But now the harvest is come by Philip's preaching.

There used to be a most bitter enmity ‹between the Jews and the Samaritans›; but now by their conversion, the Christian Jews and Samaritans are all happily united ‹in Christ›, for in Christ Jesus is neither Jew nor Samaritan, but Christ is all [one].[^004-note1403] This was a glorious instance of the wolf's dwelling with the lamb, and the leopard's lying down [with the kid].[^004-note1404]

3.[^004-note1405] The next thing to be observed is the success there was of the gospel in the calling of the Gentiles. This was a great and glorious dispensation of providence, much spoken of in the[^004-note1406] prophecies of the Old Testament, and spoken of by the apostles time after time as a most glorious event of Christ's redemption.

This was begun in the conversion of Cornelius and his family greatly to the admiration of Peter, that was used as the instrument of it, and of those that were with him, and those that were informed of it, as you may see in the Acts 10–11. And the next instances of it that we have any account [of] were in the conversions of great numbers of Gentiles in Cyprus, and Cyrene, and Antioch, by the disciples that were scattered abroad by the persecution that arose about Stephen, as we have an account in Acts 11:19–21 ["Now they which were scattered abroad … travelled as far as … Antioch.… And … spake unto the Grecians … and a great number believed, and turned to the Lord"]. And presently upon this, the disciples began to be called Christians, first at Antioch, Acts 11:26.

And after this, vast multitudes of Gentiles were converted in many different parts of the world, chiefly by the ministry of the apostle Paul, a glorious pouring out of the Spirit accompanying his preaching in one place and another. Multitudes flocked into the church of Christ in a great number of cities[^004-note1407] where the apostle came. So the number

<!-- p. 380 -->

of the members of the Christian church that were Gentiles soon far exceeded the number of its Jewish members; yea, so that in less than ten years' time after Paul was sent forth from Antioch to preach to the Gentiles, it was said of him and his companions by the Thessalonians, that they had turned the world upside down, Acts 17:6, "These men that have turned the world upside down are come hither also."[^004-note1408] But the most remarkable pouring out of the Spirit in a particular city that we have any account of in the New Testament, seems to be that in the city of Ephesus, which was a very great city. This we have an account of in the Acts 19. And there was also a very extraordinary ingathering of souls at Corinth, one of the greatest cities in all Greece, in Acts.[^004-note1409] And after this many were converted in Rome, the chief city of all the world; and the gospel was propagated into all parts of the Roman empire.[^004-note1410]

Thus the gospel sun that had lately risen on the Jews, now rose and began to enlighten the heathen world, after they had continued in[^004-note1411] gross heathenish darkness for so many ages. This was a great thing, and a new thing such as never had been seen before. All nations but the Jews, and a few that at one time and another had joined with them, had been rejected from about Moses' time. The Gentile world had been covered over with the thick darkness of gross idolatry; but now at the joyful glorious sound of the gospel they began in all parts to forsake their old idols, and abhor them, and cast them to the moles, and to the bats, and to learn to [worship] the true god, and trust in his Son, Jesus Christ.[^004-note1412] And God owned them for his people, they that had so long been far off were "made nigh by the blood of Christ."[^004-note1413] Men were changed from being heathenish and brutish to be the children of God, were called out of Satan's kingdom of darkness and brought into God's marvelous light.[^004-note1414]

And in almost all countries throughout the known world were assemblies of the people of [God], and joyful praises were sung to the true God, and Jesus Christ the glorious Redeemer. Now that great[^004-note1415] building that God began soon after the fall of man rises gloriously,

<!-- p. 381 -->

not in the same manner that it had done in former ages, but in quite a new manner. Now the prophecies of Daniel concerning the last kingdom that shall succeed the four heathenish monarchies, begins to be fulfilled; now the stone cut out of the mountain[^004-note1416] [without hands] began to smite the image [on its feet], and began to break in pieces, and to grow great, and make great advances towards filling the earth. And now God gathers together the elect from [the four winds of the earth][^004-note1417] by the preaching of the apostles and other ministers, the angles of the Christian church sent forth with the great sound of the gospel trumpet before the destruction of Jerusalem, agreeable to what Christ foretold, Matthew 24:31.

This was the success of Christ's purchase during this first period of the Christian church, which terminated in the destruction of Jerusalem.

I proceed now, in the[^004-note1418] second[^004-note1419] place, to take notice of the opposition that was made to this success of Christ's purchase by the enemies of it. Satan who lately was so ready to triumph and insult, as though he had got the victory in killing Christ, now finding himself fallen into the pit that he had digged, and finding his kingdom falling so fast, and seeing Christ's kingdom make such amazing progress such as never had been before, we may conclude he was filled with the greatest confusion and astonishment, and hell seemed to be effectually alarmed by it to make the most violent opposition against it.

And first the devil stirred up the Jews, that had before crucified Christ, to persecute the church; for 'tis observable that the persecution that the church suffered during this period was mostly amongst Jews.[^004-note1420] Thus we read in the Acts how in Jerusalem when the Holy Ghost was poured out at Pentecost, how the Jews mocked and said, "These men are full of new wine."[^004-note1421] And how the scribes and Pharisees and captain of the temple were alarmed and bestirred themselves to oppose and persecute[^004-note1422] the apostles, and first apprehended and threatened them, and afterwards imprisoned and beat them; and breathed out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the

<!-- p. 382 -->

Lord,[^004-note1423] they stoned Stephen in a tumultuous rage,[^004-note1424] and were not content to persecute those that they could find in Judea, but sent abroad to Damascus and other places to persecute all that they could find everywhere.[^004-note1425] Herod that was chief among them stretched forth his hands to vex the church, and killed James with the sword, and proceeded to take Peter also and cast him into prison.[^004-note1426]

And so in other countries we find that almost wherever the apostles came, the Jews opposed the gospel in a most malignant manner, contradicting and blaspheming. How many things did the blessed apostle Paul suffer at their hands in one place and another.[^004-note1427] How violent and bloodthirsty did they show themselves towards him when he came to bring alms to his nation;[^004-note1428] in this persecution and cruelty of theirs were fulfilled that [prophecy] of Christ, Matthew 23:34, "Behold, I send you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: [and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city]."[^004-note1429]

[^004-note1430]3.[^004-note1431] [I proceed] to take notice of those judgments that were executed on those enemies of Christ, the persecuting Jews.

1.[^004-note1432] The bulk of the people were given up to judicial blindness of mind and hardness of heart.[^004-note1433] Christ denounced such a woe upon them in the days of his flesh as Matthew 13:14–15 ["By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand.… For this people's heart is waxed gross … lest … I should heal them"].[^004-note1434] And this curse was denounced on them by the apostle Paul, Acts 28:25–27 ["Well spake the Holy Ghost.… Saying, Go unto this people, and say … seeing ye shall see, and not perceive: lest they should see with their eyes … and should be converted"]. And under this curse, this judicial blindness and hardness, they remain to this very day, having been subject to it for about seventeen hundred years: being the most awful instance of such a judgment, and monuments of God's terrible vengeance on

<!-- p. 383 -->

[them] of any people that ever were. That they should continue from generation to generation so obstinately to reject Christ, so that 'tis so rare a thing that any one of them is converted to the Christian faith, though their own scriptures of the Old Testament, which they acknowledge[^004-note1435] is so full of plain testimonies against 'em, is a remarkable evidence of their being dreadfully left of God.

2.[^004-note1436] They were rejected and cast off from being any longer God's visible people.[^004-note1437] They were broken off from the stock of Abraham, and since that have no more been reputed his seed than the Ishmaelites or Edomites that are as much his natural seed as they. The bigger part of the two tribes were now cast off, as the bulk of the ten tribes had been before, and another people taken in their room, agreeable to the predictions of their own prophets, as of Moses, Deuteronomy 32:21, "They have moved me to jealousy [with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation]"; and of Is. [Isaiah 65:1, "I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not"].[^004-note1438] They were visibly rejected and cast off by God's directing the apostles to turn away from them and let them alone, as Acts 13:45–46 ["Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles"]. And so, Acts 18:6 ["Your blood be upon your own heads.… I will go unto the Gentiles"], and Acts 28:28 ["… the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles"].

Thus far we have had[^004-note1439] the Scripture history to guide us; henceforward we shall have the guidance only of two things, viz. of Scripture prophecy and God's providence as related in human histories. But I proceed.

3.[^004-note1440] The third and last judgment on those enemies of the success of the gospel that I shall mention is the terrible destruction of their city and country by the Romans. They had great warnings and many means used with them before this destruction. First John the Baptist

<!-- p. 384 -->

warned 'em, and told 'em that the axe was laid ["unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire"].[^004-note1441] Then Christ warned them [explicitly],[^004-note1442] told them of their approaching destruction, and at the thoughts of it wept over them.[^004-note1443] And then the apostles after Christ's ascension abundantly warned them. But they proved obstinate, and went on in their opposition to Christ and his church, and their bitter persecuting practices.

Their so malignantly persecuting the apostle Paul, that we have an[^004-note1444] account of towards the latter part of the Acts, is supposed to have been not before seven or eight years before their destruction. And after this God was pleased to give 'em one more very remarkable warning by the apostle Paul in his Epistle to the Hebrews, which was an epistle written to that nation of the Jews, as is supposed, about four years before their destruction: wherein the plainest and clearest arguments are set before them from their own law, and from their prophets that they professed such a regard for, to prove that Christ Jesus must be the Son of God, and that all their law pointed to him and typified him, and that their Jewish dispensation must needs have now ceased. For though the epistle was more immediately directed to the Christian Hebrews, yet the matter of the epistle plainly shows that the Apostle intended by it the use and conviction of the unbelieving Jews. And in this epistle he particularly writes of the approaching destruction, as Hebrews 10:25, "So much the more as ye see the day approaching," and in the Hebrews 10:27 he speaks of an[^004-note1445] approaching "judgment and fiery indignation, which should devour the adversaries."

But the generality of them refusing to receive conviction, God soon destroyed them with such terrible circumstances as the destruction of no country or city since the foundation of the world can parallel, agreeable to what Christ foretold, Matthew 24:21 ["For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not from the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be"].[^004-note1446] The first destruction of Jerusalem

<!-- p. 385 -->

by the Babylonians was very terrible, as it is in a most affecting manner described by the prophet Jeremiah in his Lamentations, but this was nothing to the dreadful misery and wrath which they suffered in this destruction: God, according as Christ foretold, bringing on them all the righteous blood [that had been shed from the foundation of the world].[^004-note1447] Thus the enemies of Christ are made his footstool after his ascension, agreeable to God's promise in the Psalms 110, at the beginning ["The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool"],[^004-note1448] and Christ rules them with a rod of iron.[^004-note1449] They had been kicking against Christ, but they did but kick against the pricks,[^004-note1450] The briars and thorns set themselves [against him in battle: but he went through them, he burned them together].[^004-note1451]

This destruction of Jerusalem was in all respects agreeable to what Christ had foretold of in the Matthew 24.[^004-note1452] By the account which Josephus gives of it, that was there present and was one of the Jews that had a share in the calamity and wrote the history of that destruction. Many circumstances of this destruction greatly resembled the destruction of the wicked at the day of judgment by his account, accompanied with many fearful sights, a separation of the righteous from the wicked. Their city and temple were burnt and razed to the ground, and the city plowed, and so one stone was not ‹left upon another›, Matthew 24:2. The people ceased for the most part to be an independent government after the Babylonish captivity, the scepter departed on the death of Archelaus,[^004-note1453] ‹Judea was› made a Roman province, and then ‹they were› cast off[^004-note1454] from being a people. But now their very city and land is utterly destroyed and they carried away from it, and so have continued in their dispersions through the world for now above sixteen hundred years.

Thus there was a final end to the Old Testament world; all was finished with a kind of a day of judgment in which God's people were

<!-- p. 386 -->

saved and his enemies terribly destroyed. Thus does he that was so lately mocked, [despised, and spit upon][^004-note1455] by the Jews, and whose followers they so malignantly persecuted, appear gloriously exalted over his enemies.

<!-- p. 387 -->

### SERMON TWENTY-ONE

[^004-note1456]

> *[For the moth shall eat them up like a garment*, *and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever*, *and my salvation from generation to generation.]*

Isaiah 51:8

#### DOCTRINE

> *[The Work of Redemption is a work that God carries on from the fall of man to the end of the world.]*

HAVING shown in the forenoon[^004-note1457] how the success of Christ's purchase was carried on till the destruction of Jerusalem, I come now,

II.[^004-note1458] to show how it was carried on from that time till the destruction of the heathen empire in the time of Constantine the Great, which was the second great event that is in Scripture compared to Christ's coming to judgment. Jerusalem was destroyed about the year of our Lord 68, and so before this generation passed away that was contemporary with Christ,[^004-note1459] and it was about thirty-five years after Christ's death. The destruction of the heathen empire under Constantine was about 260 years after this.

In showing how the success of the gospel was carried on through this time I would, 1. take notice of the opposition made against it by the Roman empire, 2. how the work of the gospel went on notwithstanding all that opposition, 3. the peculiar circumstances of tribulation and distress that the church was in just before their deliverance by Constantine, 4. the great revolution in Constantine's time.

[^004-note1460]First,[^004-note1461] I would briefly show what opposition was made against the

<!-- p. 388 -->

gospel and the kingdom of Christ by the Roman empire. The opposition that was made to the gospel by the heathen Roman empire was mainly after the destruction of Jerusalem, though their opposition began before. But the opposition that was before the destruction of Jerusalem was mainly by the Jews. But when Jerusalem was destroyed, the Jews were put out of a capacity of much troubling the church now; therefore the devil turns his hand elsewhere and improves other instruments. The opposition that was made in the Roman empire against the kingdom of Christ was chiefly of two kinds.

1.[^004-note1462] They employed all their learning and philosophy and wit in opposing, as has been showed heretofore. Christ came into the world in an age wherein learning and philosophy were at their height in the Roman empire. This was employed to the utmost against the kingdom of Christ. The gospel that held forth a crucified savior was not at all agreeable to the notions of the philosophers;[^004-note1463] the Christian scheme of trusting in such a crucified redeemer appeared foolish and ridiculous to them. Greece was a country the most famous for learning of any in the Roman empire, but the Apostle observes that the doctrine of Christ crucified appeared foolishness to the Greeks, 1 Corinthians 1:23, and therefore the wise men and philosophers opposed the gospel with all the wit they had. We have a specimen of their manner of opposing in the story we have of their treatment of the apostle Paul at Athens, which was a city that had been for many ages the chief seat of philosophers of any in the whole world. We read there in the Acts 17:18[^004-note1464] that the philosophers of the Epicureans and Stoics encountered him, saying, "What will this babbler say? He seemeth to be a setter-forth of strange gods."

So they were wont to deride and ridicule Christianity. And after the destruction of Jerusalem several of these philosophers[^004-note1465] published books against it, the two chief of which were Celsus and Porphyry. These wrote books against the Christian religion with a great deal of virulence and contempt, much after the manner that the deists of the present age do oppose and ridicule Christianity. Something of their writings yet remains. As great enemies and despisers as they were of the Christian religion, yet they never denied the facts recorded of Christ and his apostles in the New Testament, the miracles that they

<!-- p. 389 -->

wrought and the like, but allowed 'em. They lived too near the times wherein these miracles were wrought to deny 'em, for they were so publicly done, and so late, that none, neither Jews nor heathens, in those days appeared to deny 'em, but laid 'em to the power of magic.

2.[^004-note1466] The authority of the Roman empire improved all their strength, time after time, to persecute entirely, if possible, to root out Christianity. This they did in[^004-note1467] ten successive general persecutions. We have heretofore observed that Christ came into the world when the strength of heathen dominion and authority was the greatest that ever it was under the Roman monarchy, the greatest and strongest human monarchy that ever was on earth. All the strength of this monarchy was employed for a long time to oppose and persecute the Christian church, and if possible to destroy it in ten successive attempts, which are called the ten heathen persecutions that were before Constantine.

The first of these, which was the persecution under Nero, was a little before the destruction of Jerusalem in which the apostle Peter was crucified and the apostle Paul beheaded soon after he wrote his second epistle to Timothy. When he wrote that epistle he was a prisoner at Rome under Nero and was soon after he wrote it beheaded, agreeable to what he says in the 2 Timothy 4:6–7, "I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I fought a good fight, I have finished [my course, I have kept the faith]."[^004-note1468] And there were many thousands of other Christians slain in that persecution.

The other nine persecutions were all after[^004-note1469] the destruction of Jerusalem. Some of these were very terrible indeed, and far exceeded the first persecution under Nero. One emperor after another set himself with the utmost rage to root out the Christian church from the earth, that there should not be so much as [the] name of Christian left in the world. And thousands and millions were they that were put to cruel deaths in these persecutions, for they spared neither sex nor age but killed 'em up as fast as they could.[^004-note1470] Under the second

<!-- p. 390 -->

general persecution, that which was next after the destruction of Jerusalem, the apostle John was banished in his old age to the isle of Patmos, where he had those visions that he has given an account of in the Revelation.[^004-note1471] Under that persecution it was reckoned that about forty thousand suffered martyrdom, which yet was nothing to what were put to death under some succeeding persecutions. Ten thousand suffered that one kind of[^004-note1472] cruel death, crucifixion, in the third persecution under the emperor Adrian. Under the fourth persecution, which began about the year of Christ 162, many suffered martyrdom in England, the land of our forefathers, where Christianity had been planted very early and, as is supposed, in the days of the apostles. And in the latter persecutions the Roman emperors, being vexed at the frustrations of their predecessors who were not able to extirpate Christianity or hinder its progress, were enraged to be the more violent in their attempts.

Thus great parts of the first three hundred years after Christ was spent in violent and cruel persecutions of the church of God by the Roman power. Satan was very unwilling to let go his hold of so great a part of the world, and every way the chief part of it, as the countries contained in the Roman empire were that he had had the quiet possession[^004-note1473] of for so many ages. And therefore when he saw it going so fast out of his hands, he bestirred himself to his utmost; all hell was, as it were, raised against it to oppose it with its utmost power. Satan thus exerting himself by the power of the heathen Roman empire is called the great red dragon in Scripture, having seven heads and ten horns, fighting against the woman clothed with the sun, in the Revelation 12[^004-note1474] of Revelation. And the terrible conflict there was between the church of Christ and the powers of the heathen empire before Constantine's time is there in verse seven represented by the war between Michael and his angels, and the dragon and his angels, "And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought."

2.[^004-note1475] I would take notice what success the gospel had in the world before Constantine's time, notwithstanding all this opposition. Though the learning and power of the Roman empire were so great, and both

<!-- p. 391 -->

were employed[^004-note1476] to the utmost against Christianity to put a stop to it and to root it out for so long a time, and in so many repeated attempts, yet all was in vain; they could neither root it out nor put a stop to it. But still in spite of all that they could do, the kingdom of Christ wonderfully prevailed, and Satan's heathen kingdom moldered and consumed away before it, agreeable to the words of the text, "The moth shall eat them up like a garment and the worm [shall eat them like wool]."[^004-note1477]

And it was very observable that, for the most part, the more they persecuted the church, the more it increased; insomuch that it became a common saying, "the blood of the martyrs is the seed of the church."[^004-note1478] Herein the church of Christ proved to be like a palm tree, of which tree it is remarked, that the greater weight is laid upon it or hung on its branches, the more it grows and flourishes; on which account, probably, the church is compared to a palm tree in Canticles 7:7, "This thy stature [is like to a palm tree]." Justin Martyr, an eminent father in the Christian church who lived in the age next[^004-note1479] after the apostles, in some writings of his that are still extant, says that in his days there was no part of mankind, whether Greeks or barbarians, or by what name soever they were called, even the most rude and unpolished nations, where prayers and thanksgivings were not made to the great creator of the world through the name of the crucified Jesus.[^004-note1480]

Tertullian, another eminent father in the Christian church who lived in the beginning of the following age, in some of his writings that yet remain,[^004-note1481] sets forth how that in his day the Christian religion had extended itself to the utmost bounds of the then known world, among which he reckons Britain, the country of our forefathers; and

<!-- p. 392 -->

thence demonstrates that the kingdom of Christ was then more extensive than any of the four great monarchies. And moreover says that, though Christians be as strangers of no long standing, yet they had filled all places of the Roman dominion, their cities, islands,[^004-note1482] castles, corporations, councils, armies, tribes; the palace, senate and courts of judicature; only they had left to those heathen their temples. And that if they should all agree to retire out of the Roman empire, the world would be amazed at the solitude and desolation that would ensue upon it there would be so few left, and that the Christians were enough to be able easily to defend themselves if they were disposed to rise up in arms against the heathen magistrates.[^004-note1483] And Pliny, an heathen author that lived in those days, says multitudes of each sex, every age and quality were become Christians, this superstition, says he, having infected and overrun not the city only, but towns and countries, the temple and sacrifices being generally desolate and forsaken.[^004-note1484]

And it was remarked by both heathen and Christian writers in those days that the famous heathen oracles in their temples where princes and others for many past ages had been wont to inquire and to receive answers with an audible voice from their gods, which were indeed[^004-note1485] answers from the devil, I say, those oracles were now silenced and struck dumb, and gave no more answers. And particularly the oracle at Delphos, which was the most famous heathen oracle in the whole world, which both Greeks and Romans used to consult, began to cease to give any answers even from the birth of Christ. And the false deity that was then worshipped there, that used to give answers from his oracle in that temple, being once inquired of why he did not now give answers as he used to do, he made this reply as Pindar an heathen author that lived in those times, gives an account. There is an Hebrew boy, says he, who is king of the gods, that has commanded me to leave this house, and to be gone to hell, and therefore you are to expect no more answers.[^004-note1486]

And many of the heathen writers that lived about that time speak

<!-- p. 393 -->

much of the oracles being silenced as a thing they wondered at, not knowing what the cause should be. Plutarch, an heathen writer of these times, wrote a particular treatise about it that is still extant.[^004-note1487] And Porphyry, one of the heathen writers before mentioned that opposed the Christian religion in his writings, has these words, "'Tis no wonder if the city for so many years has been overrun with sickness, Esculapius and the rest of the gods having withdrawn their converse with men; for since Jesus began to be worshipped no man has received any public help or benefit by the gods."[^004-note1488]

Thus did the kingdom of Christ prevail against the kingdom of Satan. I now proceed,

3.[^004-note1489] to take notice of the peculiar circumstances of tribulation and distress just before Constantine the Great came to the throne. This distress they suffered under the tenth heathen persecution which, as it was the last, so it was by far the heaviest and most severe. The church before this, after the ceasing of the ninth persecution, had enjoyed a time of godliness for about forty years together, but abusing their liberty, began to grow cold and lifeless in religion, and carnal, and contentions prevailed among 'em, by which they offended God to suffer this[^004-note1490] dreadful trial to come upon them. And Satan having lost ground so much, notwithstanding all his attempts, now seemed to bestir himself with more than ordinary rage.

Those that were then in authority set themselves with utmost violence to root out Christianity by burning all Bibles and destroying all Christians; and therefore they did not stand to try or convict them in a formal process, but fell upon them wherever they could, sometimes setting fire to houses where multitudes of them were assembled and burning them all together, and at other times slaughtering multitudes together so that sometimes their persecutors were quite spent with the labor of killing and tormenting them. And in some populous places so many were slain together that the blood ran like torrents.[^004-note1491] 'Tis related that seventeen thousand martyrs were slain in one month's space, and that during the continuance of it in the province

<!-- p. 394 -->

of Egypt alone, no less [than] 144,000 Christians died by the violence of their persecutors, besides 700,000 that died through the fatigues of banishment or the public works to which they were condemned.[^004-note1492] And this persecution lasted for ten years together, and as it [was] exceeding all foregoing persecutions in the number of martyrs, so it [was] exceeding them in the variety and multitude of inventions of torture and cruelty.[^004-note1493] Some authors that lived at that time and saw them, say they are innumerable and exceed all account and expression.[^004-note1494]

This persecution in particular was very severe in England; this persecution is foretold in the Revelation 6:9–10 ["And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?"]. And at the ten years' end, during which this persecution continued, the heathen persecutors thought they had finished their work and boasted that they had utterly destroyed the name and superstition of the Christians, and had restored and propagated the worship of the gods.

Thus it was the darkest time with the Christian church just before the break of day. They were brought to the greatest extremity just before God appeared for their glorious deliverance, as the bondage of the Israelites ‹was the most severe before their deliverance›. Their enemies thought they had swallowed[^004-note1495] them up just before their near destruction, as it was with Pharaoh and his hosts when they had hemmed in the Israelites at the Red ‹Sea›.

I come now in the,

4.[^004-note1496] [fourth] place to the great revolution that was in the world in Constantine's [time], which was in many respects like Christ's appearing in the clouds of heaven to save his people and judge the world.[^004-note1497] The people of Rome being weary of the government of those tyrants that they had lately been subject to, sent to Constantine, who

<!-- p. 395 -->

was then in the city of York in England, to come and take the throne. And being, as is said, encouraged by a vision of a pillar of light in the heavens in the form of a cross in the sight of his whole army with this inscription, *Touto nikei*, "In this you shall overcome," and the night following, by Christ's appearing to him in a dream with the same cross in his hand, [he][^004-note1498] directed him to make a cross like that to be his royal standard, that his army might fight under that banner, and assured him he should overcome.[^004-note1499] And accordingly he did, and overcame his enemies, and took possession of the imperial throne, and embraced the Christian religion, and was the first Christian emperor that ever reigned. He came to the throne about 320 years after Christ. There are several things that I would take notice of that attended or immediately followed Constantine's coming to the throne.

1.[^004-note1500] The Christian church was thereby wholly delivered from persecution. Now the day of her deliverance came after such a dark night of affliction; weeping had continued for a night, but now deliverance and joy came in the morning.[^004-note1501] Now God appeared to judge his people, and repented himself for his servants when he saw that their power was gone, and that there were none shut up or left. Christians had no persecutions now to fear, for their persecutors now were all put down, and their rulers were some of them Christians like themselves.

2.[^004-note1502] God now appeared to execute terrible judgments on their enemies. Remarkable are the accounts which history gives of the[^004-note1503] fearful ends to which the heathen emperors, and princes, and generals, and captains, and other great men came, destroying themselves in persecuting the Christians—dying miserably, one anend[^004-note1504] another, under exquisite torments of body and horrors of conscience, with a most visible hand of God upon them. So that what now came to pass might very fitly be compared to their hiding themselves in the dens and rocks of the mountains.[^004-note1505] And,

3.[^004-note1506] Heathenism now was in a great measure abolished throughout

<!-- p. 396 -->

the Roman empire. Images were now destroyed, and heathen temples pulled down, as images of gold and silver were melted down and coined into money. Some of the choicest of their idols, which were curiously wrought, were brought to Constantinople, and there drawn with ropes up and down the streets for the people to behold and laugh at. The heathen priests were dispersed and banished.

[^004-note1507]4.[^004-note1508] The Christian church was brought into a state of great peace and prosperity. Now all heathen magistrates were put down, and only Christians were advanced to places of authority, all over the empire. They had now Christian presidents, Christian governors, Christian judges and officers, instead of their old heathenish ones. Constantine set up himself to put honor on Christian bishops or ministers, and to build and adorn churches; and now large and beautiful Christian churches were erected in all parts of the world instead of the old heathen temples.

This revolution was the greatest revolution and change in the face of things on the face of the earth that ever came to pass in the world since the flood. Satan, the prince of darkness, that king and god of the heathen world, was cast out; the roaring lion was conquered by the Lamb of God in the strongest dominion that ever he had, even the Roman empire. This was a remarkable accomplishment of that [prophecy in][^004-note1509] Jeremiah 10:11, "The gods that have not made these heavens [and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens]."[^004-note1510] The chief part of the world was now brought utterly to cast off their own darkness, their old gods and old religion that they had been used to much longer than any of their histories give any account of. They had been accustomed to ‹worship the old gods› so long that they knew not any beginning of it. It was formerly spoken of as a thing unknown for a nation to change their gods, Jeremiah 2:10–11 ["Consider diligently, and see if there be such a thing. Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods?"]. But now the greater part of the nations of the known world were brought to cast off all their former gods; that multitude of gods that they worshipped were all forsaken, thousands of them were cast away for the worship of the true God and Christ the only savior. And there was a most remarkable fulfillment of that in Isaiah 2:17–18 ["And the loftiness

<!-- p. 397 -->

of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be made low: and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day. And the idols he shall utterly abolish"]. And since that, it[^004-note1511] was come to pass that those gods that were once so famous in the world, Jupiter and [others],[^004-note1512] are only heard of as things that were of old; they have no temples, no altars, no worshippers, and han't had for many hundred years.

Now is come the end of the old heathen world in the principal part of it, the Roman empire. And this great revolution and change of the state of the world, with that terrible destruction of the great men that had been persecutors, is compared in the Revelation 6 to the end of the world, and Christ coming to judgment in Revelation 6:12, and is what is most immediately signified under the sixth seal that followed; the souls under the altar crying to God ["How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?"].[^004-note1513] That by the general consent of divines and expositors has respect to this, [the downfall of the Roman empire],[^004-note1514] though it more remotely has respect to the day of judgment, or this was a type of it. The day of judgment can't be[^004-note1515] what is immediately intended, because [we have an account of] many events under [the] seventh seal.[^004-note1516] What came to pass now is also represented by the devil's being cast out of heaven to the earth.[^004-note1517]

In his great strength and glory in that mighty Roman empire he had, as it were, exalted his throne up to heaven; but now he fell like lightning from heaven and [was][^004-note1518] confined to the earth. His kingdom continued to be meaner and more barbarous nations, lower parts of the world of mankind. This is the event foretold in Revelation 12:9 etc. ["And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him"].[^004-note1519] Satan tempted Christ

<!-- p. 398 -->

and promised him to give him the glory of the kingdoms of the world, [but now he gives it to him even against his will].[^004-note1520]

This was a glorious fulfillment of that promise that God made to his Son that we have an account of in Isaiah 53:12, "Therefore will I divide [him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the Spoil with the strong]; because he hath poured out his soul [unto death: and] he was numbered with the transgressors; [and he bare the sin of many,] and made [intercession for the transgressors]."[^004-note1521] This was a great fulfillment of the prophecies of the Old Testament concerning the glorious times of the gospel, and particularly of the prophecies of Daniel. Now the kingdom of heaven is come in a glorious degree; it pleased the Lord God of heaven to set up a kingdom on the ruins of the kingdom of Satan. And such success is here of the purchase of Christ's redemption, and such honor does the Father put upon him for the disgrace he suffered when on earth. And now we see to what a height that glorious building is erected that [had] been building ever since the fall.

I will conclude at this time with an improvement of what has been said concerning the success of the gospel from Christ's ascension hitherto. And this I shall do but in this one,

INFERENCE[^004-note1522]

From what has been said we have a strong argument of the truth of the Christian religion, and that the gospel of Jesus Christ really is from God. This wonderful success of it that has been spoken of, and with those circumstances[^004-note1523] that have been mentioned, are a strong argument of it. It argues in several ways.

1.[^004-note1524] We may gather from what has been said that 'tis the gospel, and that only, that has actually been the means to bring the world to the knowledge of the true God. That they were no gods that the heathen worshipped, and that there is but only one God, is what we, now the gospel has so taught us, can see to be truth by our own

<!-- p. 399 -->

reason; it is plainly agreeable to the light of nature, it can be easily shown by reason to be demonstrably true.

The very deists themselves acknowledge that it can be demonstrated that there is one God, and but one, that only he has made and governs the world. But now 'tis evident that 'tis the gospel, and that only, that has actually been the means to bring the knowledge of this truth. It was not the instruction of philosophers; they tried in vain, "The world by their wisdom knew not God."[^004-note1525] Till the gospel and the holy Scriptures came abroad in the world, all the world lay in ignorance[^004-note1526] of the true God, and in the greatest darkness with respect to things of religion, embracing the absurdest opinions and practices that all civilized nations now acknowledge to be crazy foolishness. And so they lay one age after another, and nothing proved effectual to enlighten 'em; the light of nature, and their own reason, and all the wisdom of learned men, signified nothing till the Scriptures came. But when they came abroad, they were successful to bring the world to an acknowledgment of the one only true God, and to worship and serve him.

And hence it is that all that part of the world that now does own one only true God, Christians, Jews, Mohammedans, and even deists too, originally came by the knowledge of him. 'Tis owing to this [they] ben't in general at this day left in heathenish darkness. They have it all, first of all either immediately from the Scriptures or by tradition from their fathers, who had it first from the Scriptures. And doubtless those[^004-note1527] that now despise the Scriptures, and boast of the strength of their own reason as being sufficient to ‹bring them to knowledge of the one true God›, if the gospel had never have come abroad in the world to enlighten their forefathers, would have been as sottish and brutish idolaters, as the world in general was before the gospel came abroad. The Mohammedans that own but one true God at first borrowed the notion from the Scriptures, for the first Mohammedans were those that had been educated in the Christian religion and apostatized from it.

And this is evidential, that the Scriptures are that which God designed as the proper means to bring the world to the knowledge of himself, rather than human reason or anything else. For 'tis unreasonable to suppose that God should so order it that another means,

<!-- p. 400 -->

which God never designed as the proper means for obtaining this effect, and that only, should actually obtain; and that after human reason that he designed as the proper means have been used for a great many ages without any effect. I say, 'tis inconceivable to suppose this.[^004-note1528] If the Scriptures ben't the Word of God, then it is false, nothing else but darkness and delusion, yea and the greatest delusion that ever was. Now is it reasonable to suppose that God in his providence would make use of falsehood and delusion, and that only, to bring the world to the knowledge of himself, and no part of it ever brought to the knowledge of him any other way?

2.[^004-note1529] The gospel's prevailing as it did against such powerful opposition plainly shows the hand of God. The Roman government[^004-note1530] that did so violently set itself to harden themselves to hinder the success of the gospel, and to subdue the church of Christ, was the most powerful human government that ever was in the world. And not only so, but they seemed, as it were, to have the church in their hands. The Christians were mostly their subjects, under their command, and never took up arms to defend themselves; they did not gather together and stand in their own defense. [They] armed themselves with nothing but patience and suchlike spiritual weapons;[^004-note1531] and yet this mighty power could not conquer 'em, but on the contrary,[^004-note1532] Christianity conquered them. The Roman empire had subdued the world, they had subdued many mighty and potent kingdoms, they subdued the Grecian monarchy when they were not their subjects and made the utmost resistance; and yet they could not conquer the church that was in their hands, but on the contrary were subdued and finally triumphed over by the church.

3.[^004-note1533] No other sufficient cause can possibly be assigned of this prevailing of the gospel, but only God's own power. There is nothing else can be described as the reason of it but [this]. There was certainly some reason. Here was a great and wonderful effect, the most remarkable

<!-- p. 401 -->

change that ever was on the face of the world of mankind since the flood, and this effect was not without some cause.

Now what other cause can be directed but only the divine power? It was [not][^004-note1534] the outward strength of the instruments ‹employed in preaching the gospel›, at first only[^004-note1535] by a few fishermen, without power. It was not their craft and policy; ‹they were› illiterate. It was [not] the agreeableness of the story they had to tell to the nations and provinces of mankind; it was no pleasant fable, [but] a crucified God and savior. It was [not] the agreeableness of their doctrines to the dispositions of men.

If the power of God was what was exercised to cause the gospel to prevail, then the gospel is his word; for surely God don't use his almighty power to promote a mere imposture and delusion.

4.[^004-note1536] This success is agreeable to what Christ and his apostles foretold. "The gates of hell shall not prevail [against it]," Matthew 16:18; [^004-note1537] John 12:24, "Verily, verily, [I say unto you,] Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, [it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit]." And John 12:31–32, "Now is the judgment of this world: [now shall the prince of this world be cast out]. And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men [unto me]." John 16:8, "When the comforter is come he will convince the world [of sin, and of righteousness, and] of judgment … because [the prince of this world is judged]."[^004-note1538]

And so the apostle Paul in the 1 Corinthians 1, declares how that after "the world by wisdom [knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe]."[^004-note1539] "God chose the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and … weak things [of the world to confound the things which are mighty]; And base things [of the world, and things which are despised, … yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are]."[^004-note1540] If any foretell a thing very likely in itself to come to pass from causes that can be foreseen, 'tis no great argument. But [when a thing is

<!-- p. 402 -->

foretold that is very unlikely to come to pass, and yet it does, this is a strong argument the prediction was from God].[^004-note1541]

Thus the consideration of the manner of the propagation and success of the gospel during these times that have been spoken of afford great evidence that the Scriptures are the word of God.

<!-- p. 403 -->

### No. 9: SERMON TWENTY-TWO

[^004-note1542]

[^004-note1543]

> *[For the moth shall eat them up like a garment*, *and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever*, *and my salvation from generation to generation.]*

Isaiah 51:8

#### DOCTRINE

> *[The Work of Redemption is a work that God carries on from the fall of man to the end of the world.]*

To show how that kind of success of Christ's purchase that is obtained by the bestowment of grace on the elect church, which success is carried on from the resurrection till that first appearing [of Christ on the clouds of heaven],[^004-note1544] I say, to show how this success is carried thus, it was proposed to consider, 1. how it is carried on during the church's remaining in its afflicted state, which is from Christ's resurrection to the fall of Antichrist, and then 2. how in its state of peace and prosperity. To show how 'tis carried on through the time of its affliction and persecution from the resurrection ‹to the fall of Antichrist› it was proposed, 1. to show how it is carried ‹on› from Christ's resurrection to the destruction of Jerusalem, when ended the first great dispensation that is compared [to Christ's coming to judgment],[^004-note1545] 2. how ‹it is carried from that time till the destruction of the heathen empire in Constantine's time›, and then 3. [how it is carried on till the fall of Antichrist and the destruction of Satan's visible kingdom on earth].[^004-note1546]

<!-- p. 404 -->

[We] have gone through with the two former. I come now to show in the,

third[^004-note1547] place, how the success of Christ's redemption is carried on from the time[^004-note1548] of the overthrow of the heathen Roman empire in the time of Constantine the Great till the fall of Antichrist and the destruction of Satan's visible kingdom on earth, which is the third great dispensation that is in Scripture compared to Christ's coming to judgment. This is a period wherein many great and wonderful things are brought to pass. Herein is contained a long series of wonders of divine providence towards the Christian church. The bigger part of the book of Revelation is taken up in foretelling the events of this period.[^004-note1549] The success of Christ's purchase of redemption in this period appears mainly at the close of it when Antichrist comes to fall, when will be a far more glorious success of the gospel than ever was before, and that long series of events that are before seem to be only to prepare the way for it.

And in order to a more clear view of the great works of God in accomplishing the success of Christ's redemption and our seeing the glory of them, it will be needful as we have done in the foregoing periods to consider not only the success itself but the opposition that was made to it, and the great works of Satan in this period against the church and kingdom of Christ. And therefore in taking a view of this period I would take notice of events that may be referred to either of these heads, viz. either to the head of Satan's opposition to the success of Christ's redemption, or to the head of the success of Christ's redemption; and[^004-note1550] for the more orderly considering of the events of this period I would divide it into these four parts. The first reaching from the destruction of the heathen empire to the rise of Antichrist, the second from the rise of Antichrist to the Reformation in Luther's time, the third from thence to the present time, the fourth from the present time till Antichrist is fallen and Satan's visible kingdom on earth destroyed.

[^004-note1551]I.[^004-note1552] I would consider the events of the first part of this period reaching ‹from the destruction of the heathen empire to the rise of

<!-- p. 405 -->

Antichrist›. And here, 1. I would take notice of the opposition Satan made in this space ‹of time to the church›, 2. the success that the gospel had in it.

1.[^004-note1553] The opposition—Satan being cast out of his old heathen empire. The great red dragon, after so sore a conflict that he had had with Michael and his angels for the bigger part of three hundred years, being at last entirely routed and vanquished, so that no place was found any more in heaven for him, but he was cast down, as it were, from heaven to the earth; yet don't give over his opposition to the woman, the church of Christ, concerning which all this conflict had been. But he is still in a rage and renews his attempts, and has recourse to new devices against the church. The serpent after he is cast out of heaven to the earth, he casts out of his mouth water as a flood to cause the woman to be carried away of the flood.[^004-note1554] The opposition that he made to the church of Christ before the rise of Antichrist was[^004-note1555] principally of two sorts; it was either by corrupting the church of Christ with heresies or by new endeavors to restore paganism.

1.[^004-note1556] I would observe that after the destruction of the heathen Roman empire, Satan infested the church with heresies, though there had been so glorious a work of God in delivering his church from her heathen persecutors and overthrowing the heathen empire, yet the day of the church's travail not being ended and the set time of her prosperity not being yet come, as being what was to succeed the fall of Antichrist. The peace and prosperity that the church enjoyed in Constantine's time was but very short; it was a respite that gave the church a time of a peace or silence, as it were, for half an hour, wherein the four angels held the four winds from blowing till the servants of God could be sealed on their foreheads.[^004-note1557] But the church soon began to be greatly infested with heresies, the two principal and those that did most infest the church were[^004-note1558] the Arian and Pelagian heresies.

The Arians began soon after Constantine came to the throne. They denied the doctrine of the Trinity, and denied the divinity of Christ

<!-- p. 406 -->

and the Holy Ghost, and maintained that they were but mere creatures. This heresy increased more and more in the church, and prevailed like a flood that threatened to overflow all and entirely carry away the church of [God]; insomuch that before that age was out, that is, before the fourth century or hundred years after Christ was finished, the bigger part of the Christian world were become Arians. There were some emperors, the successors of Constantine, that were Arians; so that the Arians being the prevailing party, and having the civil authority of their side, did raise a great persecution against the true church of Christ. So that this heresy might well be compared to a flood out of the mouth of the serpent, that threatened to overflow all and quite carry away the woman.[^004-note1559]

The Pelagian heresy arose in the beginning of the next century, or hundred years after[^004-note1560] Christ. It began by one Pelagius that was born in Britain; his British name was Morgan. He denied original sin, and held the power of free will, and denied the influence of the Spirit of God in conversion, and held many other things of like tendency; and this heresy did for a while greatly infest the church. Pelagius' principal antagonist that wrote in defense of the orthodox was St. Augustine.

2.[^004-note1561] The other kind of opposition that Satan made against the church was in his endeavors to restore paganism.

1.[^004-note1562] And his first attempt to restore paganism in the Roman empire was by Julian the Apostate. Julian was nephew to Constantine the Great, and became emperor. When Constantine died, he left his empire to his three sons, and [when] they were dead, Julian the Apostate reigned in their stead. He had been a professed Christian; but he fell from Christianity and turned pagan, and[^004-note1563] therefore is called "the apostate." When he came to the throne he used his utmost endeavors to overthrow the Christian church, and set up paganism again in the empire. He put down the Christian magistrates and set up heathen ones in their room, he rebuilt the heathen temples and set up the heathen worship in the empire, and became a most notorious persecutor of the Christians, and as is thought, against his light, he used

<!-- p. 407 -->

to call Christ by way of reproach, the Galilean. He was killed with a lance in his wars with the Persians. When he see he was mortally wounded, he took an handful of his blood and threw it up towards heaven, crying out, "Thou hast overcome, O Galilean."[^004-note1564] And he is commonly thought by divines to have committed the unpardonable sin.[^004-note1565]

[^004-note1566]2.[^004-note1567] Another way that Satan attempted to restore paganism in the Roman empire was by the invasions and conquests of heathen nations. For in this space of time that we are upon the Goths and Vandals and other heathen barbarous nations that dwelt in the north of the Roman empire invaded the empire and obtained great conquests, and even overran the empire, and in the fifth century, or five hundred years after Christ, took the city of Rome. And they finally subdued and conquered ad took possession of the western empire, as it was called, or the western half of the empire, and divided it amongst them, divided it into ten kingdoms with which began the ten horns of the beasts; for we are told the ten horns are ten kings [who] shall rise in the latter part of the Roman empire.[^004-note1568] These are also represented by the ten toes of Nebuchadnezzar's image.[^004-note1569] The invasion and conquests of these heathen nations[^004-note1570] are supposed to be foretold in the eighth chaper of Revelation, in what came to pass under the sounding of the our first trumpets.[^004-note1571]

Now these nations that now took possession of the western empire were heathens, so that by their means heathenism was again for a while restored after it had been rooted out.

[^004-note1572]So much for the opposition of Satan against ‹the church› during this space before the rise of Antichrist. I proceed,

<!-- p. 408 -->

2.[^004-note1573] to show what success there was of the gospel in this space notwithstanding[^004-note1574] this opposition. And here,

1.[^004-note1575] I would observe that the opposition of Satan in these things was baffled. Though the dragon cast out of his mouth such a flood after the woman to carry her away, yet he could not attain his design; but the earth helped the woman, and opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood that the dragon cast out of his mouth.[^004-note1576] These heresies that for a while so much prevailed, yet after a while dwindled away, and orthodoxy was again restored, and that attempt by Julian was baffled at his death.[^004-note1577]

2.[^004-note1578] The gospel during this space of time was further propagated amongst many barbarous heathen nations in the confines of the Roman empire. In Constantine's time there was a considerable propagation of the gospel in the East Indies, chiefly by the ministry of one Frumentius.[^004-note1579] Great numbers of the Iberians, a heathen people, were converted to Christianity by a Christian woman of eminent piety[^004-note1580] that they had taken captive. And the same account is given of several other barbarous nations that were at war with the Roman empire, that great numbers of them were brought to receive the gospel by teaching and example of captives that they had taken in war. And after this, about the year of Christ 372, the gospel was propagated among a barbarous people that dwelt in Arabia, as it was also among some of the northern nations, as particularly a prince of the country of the Goths about this time became Christian, and a great number of his people with him. Towards the latter end of this century, the gospel was further propagated among the Persians, and also the Scythians, a barbarous

<!-- p. 409 -->

people that the Apostle mentions, Colossians 3:11, "Barbarian, Scythian."[^004-note1581] And after this, about the year 430, there was a remarkable conversion of a heathen people called the Burgundians to the Christian faith. About the same time, the gospel began in this age to be propagated in Ireland, and the Irish that till then had been heathens, began to receive the Christian faith. About the same time, it was further propagated among some [of] the barbarous people in Scotland, and also some other places. In the next century to this, one Zathus, a heathen king that ruled over a people called the Colchians, was brought to renounce[^004-note1582] his heathenism and embrace the Christian religion.[^004-note1583] Several other barbarous nations are recorded to have renounced heathenism and embraced Christianity about this time, that I cannot stand to mention.[^004-note1584]

Thus I have briefly considered the principal events of providence that concern the success of the gospel of Christ from Constantine to the rise of Antichrist. I come now to the,

[^004-note1585]II.[^004-note1586] second part of the space of time from Constantine to the destruction of Antichrist, viz. that which reaches from the rise of Antichrist before the Reformation by Luther and others. And this is the darkest and most dismal day that ever the Christian church saw, and probably the darkest that ever it will see. The time of the church's affliction and persecution, as was observed before, is from Christ's resurrection till the destruction of Antichrist, excepting where the day is, as it were, shorted by some intermissions and times of respite, which God gives for the elect's sake. But this time, from the rise of

<!-- p. 410 -->

Antichrist till the Reformation, was a space wherein the Christian church was in its greatest depth of depression and its darkest time of all.

The true church in this space was for many hundred years in a state of great obscurity, like the woman in the wilderness,[^004-note1587] indeed almost hid from sight and observation. In speaking of the events of this space of time I would, 1. take notice of the great machinations[^004-note1588] and works of the devil against the kingdom of Christ during this time, and 2. how the church of Christ was upheld during this time.

1.[^004-note1589] I would take notice of the great works of the devil against the kingdom of Christ during this time. Satan had done great things against the Christian church before but had been baffled once and again. Michael and his angels had obtained a glorious victory. How terrible was his opposition during the continuance of the heathen empire, and how glorious was Christ's victory and triumph over him in Constantine's time. It pleased God now so to prepare the way for a yet more glorious victory over him, to suffer him to renew his strength, and to make his interests strong in the world, and do the utmost that his power and subtilty can help him to; and suffers him to have a long time to lay his scheme, and to establish his interest, and make his numbers strong; and suffers him to carry his designs a great[^004-note1590] length indeed, to the almost swallowing up his church, and to a high and proud and almost uncontrolled dominion in the world: a long time before Christ finally conquers and subdues and utterly ruins his visible kingdom on earth, as he will do in the time of the destruction of Antichrist; thus gloriously triumphing over him after he has done the utmost that his power and subtilty can extend to, and showing that he is above him after he has dealt most proudly and lifted himself highest of all.

The two great works of the devil that he in this space of time wrought against the kingdom of Christ are his erecting his Antichristian and Mohammedan kingdoms, which have been and still are two kingdoms of great extent and strength, both together swallowing up the ancient Roman empire; the kingdom of Antichrist swallowing up the western empire, and Satan's Mohammedan kingdom the eastern empire. As the Scriptures in the book of Revelation represents it, 'tis

<!-- p. 411 -->

in the destruction of these that the glorious victory of Christ at the introduction[^004-note1591] of the glorious times of the church will mainly consist; and here let us briefly observe how Satan erects and maintains these and two great kingdoms of his in opposition to the kingdom of Christ. And,

1.[^004-note1592] Of the kingdom of Antichrist.[^004-note1593] This seems to be the masterpiece of all the contrivances of the devil against the kingdom of Christ, and is evidently so spoken of in Scripture; and therefore Antichrist is the man of sin or "that man of sin," 2 Thessalonians 2:3. He is so called emphatically as though he were so eminently. 1 John 2:18, so he is called the "Antichrist,"[^004-note1594] which signifies the opponent or adversary of Christ. Not that he is the only opponent of Christ; there were many others besides he. The apostle John observes that in his days there were many Antichrists; but yet this is called the Antichrist as though there were none but he, because he was so eminently and above all others. So this contrivance of the devil is called "the mystery of iniquity," 2 Thessalonians 2:7. And we find no enemy of Christ one-half so much spoken of in the prophecies of Revelation as this, and the destruction of no enemy spoken [of] as so glorious and happy for the church. The craft and subtilty of the devil above all appears in this work of his, as might be shown were it not that it would be too long.

This is a contrivance of the devil to turn the ministry of the Christian church into a ministry of the devil, and to turn these angels of the church into fallen angels and so into devils; and in the tyranny and superstition and idolatry and persecution that he sets up, to make an image of ancient paganism,[^004-note1595] and more than to restore what was lost in the empire by the overthrow of paganism in Constantine's time. So that by this means the head of the beast that was wounded unto death in Constantine has his deadly wound healed in Antichrist, Revelation 13:3; and the dragon that formerly reigned in the heathen Roman empire being cast out thence, after the beast with seven heads and ten horns rises in his room, gives him his power and seat and great authority, and all the world wonders after the beast.[^004-note1596]

<!-- p. 412 -->

[^004-note1597]I am far from pretending to determine the time when the reign of Antichrist began, which is a point that has been so much controverted among divines and expositors.[^004-note1598] 'Tis certain that the 1260 days—years that are so often in Scripture mentioned as the time of the continuance of Antichrist's reign—did not commence before the year of Christ 479.[^004-note1599] Because if they did, they would have ended, and Antichrist would have fallen before now. But I shall [not] pretend to determine precisely how long it was after this that that period began.

[^004-note1600]The rise of Antichrist was gradual. The Christian church corrupted itself in many things presently after Constantine's time, growing more and more superstitious in its worship, by degrees bringing in many ceremonies into the worship of God, till at length they brought in the worship of saints and set up images in their churches, and the clergy usurped more,[^004-note1601] and the bishop of Rome gradually assuming more and more authority to himself. In the primitive times he was only a minister of a congregation, then a standing moderator of a presbytery, then a diocesan bishop, then a metropolitan which was equivalent to an archbishop, then he was a patriarch, then afterwards he claimed the power of universal bishop over the whole Christian church through the world, wherein he was opposed for a while but afterwards was confirmed in it by the civil power of the emperor in the year 606. After that he claimed the power of a temporal prince, and so was wont to carry two swords to signify that both the temporal and spiritual sword was his, and claimed more and more authority. Till at length he, as Christ's vicar on earth, claimed the very same power that Christ would have if he was presently on earth and reigned on his throne, or the same power that belongs to God, and used to be called God on earth, and used to be submitted to by[^004-note1602] all

<!-- p. 413 -->

the princes of Christendom. He claimed power to crown princes and degrade them at his pleasure, and this power was owned. And it came to this, that kings and emperors used to kiss his feet. The emperors were wont to receive their crowns at his hands.

And princes were wont to dread the Pope's displeasure, as they would dread a thunderbolt from heaven; for if the Pope was pleased to excommunicate a prince, all his subjects were at once freed from their allegiance to him, and not only, yea, and obliged not to own him any more on pain of excommunication. But any man might kill him wherever he find him. And not only so, but he was believed to have power to damn men at pleasure; for whoever died under his excommunication was looked upon as certainly damned. And several emperors were actually deposed and ejected and died miserably by his means. And if the people, if the people of any state or kingdom, did not please him,[^004-note1603] he had power to lay that state or kingdom under an

<!-- p. 414 -->

interdict, which was a sentence pronounced by the Pope against that state and kingdom whereby all sacred administrations among them could have no validity. There could be no valid baptisms, or sacraments, or prayers, or preachings, or pardons, till that interdict was taken off; so that that people remained in their apprehension in a miserable damnable state, and therefore dreaded it as they would a storm of fire and brimstone from heaven. Other princes in order to execute their wrath on a prince or people they were displeased with must be put to a great deal of trouble.

The heathen Roman emperors therefore [were] the most powerful secular princes, but [now the power of the Roman popes exceeded theirs].[^004-note1604] And as the Pope and his clergy robbed the people of their ecclesiastical and civil rights[^004-note1605] and privileges, so also they robbed them of their estates, and drained all Christendom of their money, and engrossed the most of their riches into their own coffers by their vast revenues besides pay for pardons, and indulgences, baptisms, extreme unction, and deliverance out of purgatory, and an hundred other things. And cruel were his persecutions; see how well this agrees with the prophecies, 2 Thessalonians 2:3–4; Daniel 7:20–21; Revelation 13:5–7; Revelation 17:3–4.

During this time also, superstition and ignorance more and more prevailed. The holy Scripture by degrees was taken out of the hands of the laity, the better to promote ‹the privileges of the clergy›. And instead of promoting knowledge among the people, they industriously promoted ignorance, ignorance, the mother of devotion. And so great was the darkness that learning almost ceased out of the world—the very priests themselves, most of 'em, barbarously ignorant as to any commendable learning or any other knowledge than their hellish craft in oppressing and tyrannizing over the souls of the poor people.[^004-note1606] The superstition and wickedness of the church of Rome kept growing worse and worse, till the very time of the Reformation.

And the whole Christian world were led away into this great defection, excepting the remains of the Christian churches in the eastern empire that had not been utterly overthrown by the Turks, as the Greek churches and some others who were also sunk into great darkness and gross superstition, excepting also those few that were

<!-- p. 415 -->

the people of God that are represented by the woman in the wilderness and God's two witnesses,[^004-note1607] of which afterwards.

This is one of those two great kingdoms that the devil in this period erected in opposition to the kingdom of Christ, and was the greatest and chief. I come now,

2.[^004-note1608] To speak of the other, the second, which is in many respects like unto it, which is[^004-note1609] his Mohammedan kingdom which is another great kingdom of mighty power and vast extent that Satan set up against the kingdom of Christ. He set this up in the eastern empire as he did that of Antichrist in the western.

Mohammed was born in the year of Christ 622[^004-note1610] in Arabia. When he was about forty years of age, he began to give forth that he was the great prophet of God and began to teach his new invented religion, of which he was to be worshipped as the head next under God. [He] published his Alcoran, which he pretended he received from the angel Gabriel. And being a subtile crafty man, and possessed of considerable wealth, and living amongst a people that were very ignorant and greatly divided in their opinions of religious matters by his subtilty and fair promises of a sensual paradise, he gained a number to be his followers and set up for their prince, and propagates his religion by the sword, and made it meritorious of paradise to fight for him.
